title: POC - Sensitive Pathways & Ephemeralization Strategy Kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share PII/redaction playbook and regex examples (Liam) by 2027-10-08
Customer to provide sample anonymized logs and 2 example prompt flows (Tara) by 2027-10-12
SE to run baseline latency + throughput bench on customer's sample workload and share CSV (Priya) by 2027-10-15
Schedule pilot kick-off demo with SOC/compliance on 2027-10-19 (Sofia)
action_items: Liam Chen: Share ephemeral prompt storage matrix + config recommendations (due 2027-10-08)
Tara Nguyen: Upload 3 sanitized prompt examples and 1 spike workload (due 2027-10-12)
Priya Desai: Run 10k-request throughput bench (quantized model + batch sizes) and send results (due 2027-10-15)
Marcus Osei: Provide PaloVista retention policy doc and encryption key rotation schedule (due 2027-10-11)
summary: Kickoff to define success criteria and POC scope for handling sensitive data paths. Main themes: ephemeral prompt options vs long-term storage, redaction heuristics, retention windows, KMS integration, and workload sizing for latency/throughput benchmarks. Agreement to run an initial bench using provided sample traffic and to trial an ephemeral-only storage profile for sensitive flows.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intro round — we'll go through scope, success criteria, and then bench plan. can everybody state their role?
[00:10] Karen (PaloVista): yea hi, Karen Li — head of data at PaloVista. we run a claims triage assistant, lots of SSNs, policy numbers in prompts so privacy is a huge concern.
[00:22] Marcus (PaloVista Sec): Marcus here, security architect — mainly around encryption, key management, and auditability.
[00:28] Tara (PaloVista ML): Tara — ml eng, i'll provide sample prompt flows and will run some local data sanitization.
[00:34] Liam: great. Priya, Marco — quick intros?
[00:37] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya Desai, SE. i'll own the benching and the integration play for private deployment and hosted fallback.
[00:42] Marco (Redwood): Marco Alvarez, solution architect — focus on KMS, VPC connectivity, and config to make prompt ephemeralization possible.
[00:48] [00:50] Liam: ok quick agenda: 1) define success criteria for the POC, 2) agree workload size + bench plan, 3) data handling (redaction/retention/ephemeral), 4) timeline and owners.
[00:58] Karen: for success criteria, business wants: less than 150ms p50 gen latency for our short prompts, p95 under 400ms during normal usage, and no more than 0.5% of outputs with PII leakage in our test set. also retention must comply with our policy — default TTL for prompts 7 days but sensitive flows zero retention unless explicitly flagged.
[01:20] Priya: ok note — our hosted offering has ephemeral-only mode for prompts for certain routes, and we can alloy a persisted mode for lower-sensitivity flows. ephemeral basically means no disk writes and only short-living keys in RAM with a TTL.
[01:35] Marcus: important — ephemeral mode is fine but we need audit logs (who called, route, model, tokens) without storing prompt content. is that possible?
[01:44] Marco: yes we can emit metadata-only audit events to your SIEM — request id, user id hash, model used, token counts, latency, but redact prompt text and response content. that lives in a separate telemetry stream that never contains raw prompts.
[01:56] Karen: how do you technically redacted PII? we rely on regex and a fingerprinting step — we need to see examples.
[02:04] Priya: we support a redaction pre-processor hook. typical approach: first pass through an entity detector (custom models or rules), mask high-confidence SSN/email/card numbers, optionally hash or token-replace them. we can also integrate your existing PII detector via API. caveat: noisy transcriptions sometimes mis-id—we'll show examples.
[02:28] Tara: i want to avoid over-redaction — we still need some context for the model to answer. any suggestions on best practice?
[02:34] Priya: yeah, we recommend structured placeholders with type hints like [SSN_REDACTED-type=ssn] so the model still knows the entity class but not the actual value. that preserves downstream accuracy.
[02:44] [03:00] Liam: benching — we need to size workload. Tara, what's your expected QPS and token counts?
[03:05] Tara: for claims triage the steady state is ~35 RPS, peak to 200 RPS for flash events. average prompt length is 120 tokens, responses ~60 tokens. we have a 2k daily spike pattern.
[03:18] Priya: ok for bench plan we'll run: 1) steady load 35 RPS for 30 minutes, 2) 5 minute peak at 200 RPS, 3) long-tail test with mixed sequence lengths to measure KV cache effects. we'll run both quantized and FP16 variants to show token cost and latency tradeoffs.
[03:40] Marcus: any concern about KV cache storing sensitive context?
[03:44] Marco: good call — KV cache lives in GPU memory and is per-session. for ephemeral routes we can zero the KV cache after response or disable caching entirely. for non-sensitive routes we keep caching to reduce latency.
[03:55] Karen: retention — we have a legal requirement to keep minimal metadata for audits for 3 years but content cannot be stored beyond 7 days without explicit consent.
[04:06] Marcus: also need key rotation and HSM backed KMS. we cannot have vendor-managed keys without customer control.
[04:12] Marco: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys in Private deployments; for Hosted we do bring-your-own-KMS via an envelope encryption approach — you provide key material, we never log plaintext keys.
[04:23] Priya: to align with your audit needs we can stream redacted telemetry to your Splunk/Datadog and provide signed audit snapshots.
[04:31] [04:40] Tara: on metrics for success — beyond latency/PII leakage we want: accuracy delta <= 3% compared to baseline model, and cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll share internal target).
[04:51] Liam: noted. we'll include quality evals on the prompt set you provide. quality monitoring will be part of the POC — we can run n-gram overlap plus some human review on a 200-sample set.
[05:05] Karen: about flow — can we trial ephemeral-only for our high-sensitivity routes and persisted for others? we want to measure both.
[05:12] Marco: yes — config is per-route. we can set retention TTL at route level, have ephemerality flag, and toggle redaction pre-processors.
transcript_continued:
[05:30] Priya: instrumentation for bench — we'll need: 1) a synthetic workload or your replay logs (sanitized), 2) expected concurrency and user-id hashing scheme, 3) preferred models to test (we recommend a mid-size quantized for cost baseline and a FP16 for low-latency).
[05:48] Tara: we'll sanitize logs and provide a 24-hour replay plus one spike. we may need help anonymizing—Marcus can handle removal of direct identifiers but we want to keep structural tokens.
[06:02] Marcus: yes we'll produce a sanitized sample with hashes for uuids and masked SSNs per your regex patterns.
[06:09] Liam: timeline — propose: data handoff by 2027-10-12, bench run 2027-10-13 to 10-15, results review 2027-10-16, compliance demo 2027-10-19, then pilot sign-off by 2027-10-26. feasible?
[06:22] Karen: aggressive but reasonable, sign-off requires legal and SOC folks to see audit logs.
[06:27] Marcus: we'll need the security docs — SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, and proof of key isolation for the hosted path.
[06:34] Liam: we'll send Redwood security pack and SOC2 Type II report link. also will include a short guide on ephemeralization config.
[06:41] Karen: curious about escape cases — if our redactor misses a phone number inside a poorly transcribed chunk, what about post-hoc redaction?
[06:49] Priya: we support a post-ingest redaction job that re-processes stored artifacts; for ephemeral routes there's nothing to re-process since we don't persist content. for persisted flows we can run periodic sweeps and redact retroactively, and purge logs as needed.
[07:03] Tara: how do you measure PII leakage? we need an automated evaluation metric.
[07:08] Priya: we'll run a leakage detection step: run an NER model over outputs and compare against ground-truth entities; false negatives are flagged. we'll provide a leakage score and example leaks. plus manual review sample.
[07:18] Liam: ok final recap: Redwood will share redaction examples, ephemeral config doc, security pack, and run benches after PaloVista hands off sanitized logs. PaloVista will provide sanitized dataset, retention policy, and reviewers. next meeting to review bench results on 2027-10-16.
[07:35] Karen: thanks — please send pricing for dedicated vs hosted lanes for the pilot.
[07:40] Liam: will do. thanks everyone.
[07:45] [07:50] (call ends)
